name: Opus Broadening
strategy: Long the current cross-sectional momentum leaders in software/semis/fintech, short two persistent laggards, with per-name stops - betting winners keep winning and losers keep losing.

positions.thesis: Pressed 20->24 and still the largest position. The reason to add is that the basis of the trade changed from technical to structural since I opened it: what I bought as a violent reversal off an SK Hynix miss is now underwritten by SK Hynix's own chairman guiding global memory supply roughly 20% below demand through 2030, Micron HBM sold out through 2027, Kioxia's entire 2026 NAND output committed, and record global semi sales of $120.6B in May, the fifteenth consecutive monthly record. SOXQ is +123% over one year, first in my universe on twelve-month-minus-one-month momentum. Still taken via the diversified ETF at 2bps rather than Micron at $878 after a $110-$1,255 annual range, because I want the sector and not the gap risk. Stop stays wide at -18% because the complex still trades in 15-20% weekly swings.

Up 14->18. Closed at $330.49 against a 52-week high of $331.40 - 99.7% of its range, the best relative-strength reading in my universe and the literal definition of the signal my mandate trades. Two things improved since I set the weight: the earnings date moved from Aug 26 to Sept 2, so the print my stop was sized against is no longer inside my holding window, and Wells Fargo took its target to $500 on agent adoption. Cortex AI Gateway extends the consumption story that lets me own the AI capex cycle through software rather than hardware. Stop stays at -22% because a name at 156x forward and 100% of its range has no valuation floor to land on.

Up 12->15. At $363.86 on a $139.57-$376.98 range it sits at 94% of range with market cap up 157% year to date, and BofA, Barclays and Oppenheimer all raised targets. The specific unlock is that earnings moved from Aug 17 to Sept 1, which removes the print I was explicitly holding size back for. China's formal security review is the live negative and the reason this is a 15 and not a 20; the sell-side reads it as noise against AI-driven security demand, and security budgets are the least discretionary line in enterprise software when the labour market is cracking. Stop stays real at -20% against a 352 trailing P/E.

New. Rose 10.32% on 8/7 to $172.01 and is up roughly 30% since Q2, on trailing revenue of $6.16B growing 79% with EPS up 288%, driven by commercial AI acceleration rather than government renewals alone. A large positive post-earnings move on an accelerating fundamental is the cleanest fresh momentum ignition available to me, and post-announcement drift is the same effect my mandate is built on. It adds a driver I do not already own - defense and government AI software, uncorrelated to both memory pricing and enterprise data consumption - so it is diversification inside the mandate rather than more of SMH. Sized at only 10% because at 65% of a $106-$208 range it has not reclaimed its high, it carries a 147 P/E, and a 1.56-beta name that just moved 30% can give a third of it back without anything being wrong.

Unchanged at 6% and untraded. At roughly $90.71 on a $63.52-$153.86 range it is at 30% of range and 41% below its high despite a record quarter - $1.3B revenue up 32%, $22B net deposits - and Cantor cut its target from $130 to $115 anyway. A name that cannot hold a bid on a blowout print, through a week when the Nasdaq made a record high and the whole retail-risk complex should have carried it, is a laggard confirming itself; that non-participation in this specific week is the new evidence. Kept small with a wide -25% stop because it is a high-beta retail and crypto proxy that squeezes hardest in exactly the melt-up my longs need.

Cut 8->4, reversing last week's upsize. The fundamental case is intact and arguably worse: -$23.7B free cash flow, $97.6B net debt, S&P at BBB- one notch off junk, ~$40B of FY27 debt and equity financing needed, all against a $638B backlog worth 1.6x the market cap that still has to convert to cash, and at $147 on a $114.50-$345.72 range it remains a bottom-decile twelve-month momentum name. What changed is the tape, not the balance sheet - a Google Cloud and Gemini tie-up, a $7B defense contract and Oracle Health expansion took it up roughly 16% in a week, one session of it +9%. My mandate wants two persistent laggards and this is still one, and the reversal is the recent month that momentum construction deliberately ignores. But being right slowly at 8% with a -20% stop a few points away is a coin flip on timing, so I hold the view at a size where the stop costs 0.8% of NAV.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-08: Two problems, both mine rather than the market's. First, ORCL. I upsized the short 5->8 on the argument that a capex boom hurts the one participant who has to borrow to build. Within days it went from roughly $126 to $147 - one +9% session, about +16% against me on the week - on a Google Cloud and Gemini integration, a $7B defense contract, Oracle Health expansion and new logo wins. It is now within a few points of my -20% stop. The mandate case for keeping it is real and unchanged: at $147 on a $114.50-$345.72 range it is at 14% of range, free cash flow is -$23.7B, net debt $97.6B, S&P has it at BBB- and it needs ~$40B of FY27 financing - on twelve-month-minus-one-month momentum, the construction my mandate uses, it is bottom decile and this bounce is precisely the recent-month reversal that construction skips. But a thesis that draws a 16% counter-move inside a week has earned a smaller position, not the bigger one I gave it. I cut it to 4%, where the stop caps the leg at 0.8% of NAV, and I stop pressing a loser to prove a point. Second, I was carrying 40% cash under a mandate that says winners keep winning, through the strongest week for the indices since April, and every one of my three longs got stronger while I sat in T-bills. That is the mandate not being expressed. SNOW closed at $330.49 against a 52-week high of $331.40 and its earnings moved out to Sept 2, so the event risk I sized my stop for is not in my window. PANW is at 94% of its range with its print also moved to Sept 1. Semis are no longer a squeeze I got lucky on - SK Hynix now guides global memory supply ~20% below demand through 2030, Micron HBM is sold out through 2027 and Kioxia's whole 2026 NAND book is committed, which is a multi-year shortage, and SOXQ is +123% over one year. I press all three and add PLTR, where a +30% post-earnings move on 79% trailing revenue growth is the freshest momentum ignition in my universe with the print already behind it. I add no fintech long on purpose: I screened NU at 24% of its range, AFRM at 57% and HOOD at 30%, and a sector with no leader supplies a short, not a long - which is where my fintech exposure already sits. I keep 23% cash rather than going flat out, because -23,000 payrolls with 103,000 revised away is a real crack and this is a book of 150x-to-350x-earnings names at record index highs.
novelty: Round 3 shares zero symbols with Round 2 and the two books are structurally opposed rather than merely different: Round 3 is 67% long concentrated megacap-adjacent AI software and semis, while Round 2 is short QQQ and long equal-weight, small-cap, biotech, industrials, banks and energy - same-direction gross-weight overlap is 0%, and the one place they touch the same theme they touch it on opposite sides.
research_notes:
WEEK TAPE (through 2026-08-07 close): S&P 500 +3.6% to a record 7,757.64; Nasdaq Composite +5.2% to a record 26,690.62; Dow +~3%. Strongest week for the majors since mid-April. Treasury yields FELL.

MACRO — the decisive item. July nonfarm payrolls printed -23,000 against +80,000 expected (range 10k-140k). Local government education -50k, retail -19k, leisure/hospitality -40k (World Cup roll-off), health care +22k. Revisions were worse than the headline: May cut 129k -> 63k, June cut 57k -> 20k, ~103k removed between them. CME FedWatch: September hike odds fell 57% -> 44% within hours; hold-in-September rose to 56.1%. This is the direct inversion of the hawkish premise (three hike dissents, 30-yr at 5.22%/2007 highs) that I underwrote my Round 2 book on seven days ago.

ENERGY — premise decayed. WTI $77.08 on 8/7 (-0.27%), Brent $82.15. Iran and Oman are negotiating over the Strait of Hormuz; the Jordan-strike war premium that justified taking energy to 25% of Round 2 has largely come out. Breadth internals weak too: only 33% of XLE/XOP/OIH holdings above the 10-day SMA, 38% of XLE names on a Buy technical.

SEMIS — squeeze became structure. SOXQ $97.20, +123.4% over one year. SMH $571.82 (8/6). Semi ETFs surged up to 19% on the week. The driver is now supply, not a short squeeze: SK Hynix chairman guides global memory supply ~20% BELOW demand through 2030, Micron HBM sold out through 2027, Kioxia's entire 2026 NAND output committed, global semi sales a record $120.6B in May (+104% y/y, 15th straight record month). BofA reiterated $1,550 on Micron. This is confirmation of the reversal I acted on last week.

MY ROUND 3 NAMES. SNOW $330.49 (+3.93% on 8/7) against a 52-week high of $331.40 — 99.7% of range, an outright momentum leader; Wells Fargo raised PT to $500; Cortex AI Gateway launched; earnings moved OUT to 2026-09-02, so no print inside my window. PANW $363.86, 52wk $139.57-$376.98 = 94% of range, market cap +157% YTD, BofA to $420; China opened a formal security review (analysts treat as noise); earnings moved to 2026-09-01. ORCL $147.02, 52wk $114.50-$345.72 = 14% of range but UP ~16% off its 7/29 close (one +9% session) on a Google Cloud/Gemini tie-up, a $7B defense contract and Oracle Health expansion; fundamentals unchanged and ugly (-$23.7B FCF, $97.6B net debt, S&P cut to BBB-, ~$40B FY27 raise planned, Burry re-shorting). HOOD ~$90.71 close, 52wk $63.52-$153.86 = 30% of range, 41% below its high despite record Q2 ($1.3B rev +32%, $22B net deposits); Cantor cut PT $130 -> $115.

FINTECH SCREEN — no leader exists. NU $13.84 on a $11.20-$18.98 range = 24% of range, 27% below its high. AFRM $75.25 on $42.10-$100.00 = 57% of range. HOOD 30%. Under a cross-sectional momentum mandate that names fintech, the honest read is that the sector supplies a short, not a long. I am not forcing a fintech long.

ROUND 2 NAMES. RSP $220.09 against a 52-week high of $221.09 — equal weight is at a record and net inflows are accelerating; the anti-concentration long is working even though the anti-concentration SHORT is not. XBI $157.37, 52wk $84.52-$165.71 = 90% of range, +83.6% over one year, +2.87% on 8/7, equal-weighted by construction. Russell 2000 +20% YTD, best year since 2003; ~40% of constituents carry floating-rate debt, which is exactly why a payroll miss that kills hike odds is a small-cap catalyst.

CANDIDATE I REJECTED: MU $877.57 — 12-1 momentum is enormous (from $110) and forward P/E is 6.1, but it sits 30% below its $1,255 high, took a hit on SanDisk guidance, and I already own it inside SMH. Adding it is concentration with single-name gap risk, not new signal.

STANDING-ORDER TAPE CHECK: 12 of 17 fills ever were shorts in GDX/GDXJ and SOXL being stopped out, five on 8/07 alone. I am short neither complex — I am LONG semis via SMH — so that warning cuts in my favour rather than against me. None of my own stops fired this week.
